title: Cluster topography
summary: Using the LP algebraic toolkit, Conway's original topograph is rethought of as a cluster construction, paving the way for a wider topography based on mutation-type local rules. As a remarkable application of such cluster-driven upgrade, both the process of analytic continuation for Painlevé VI and the reduction algorithm for quadratic forms are endowed with the Laurent phenomenon. En passant, the rattlesnake is defined so to complete the bijection between snake graphs and rationals to the whole of $\mathbb{Q}$.
